simple.meaning: בָּכָא (bâkâʼ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “the weeping tree (some gum-distilling tree, perhaps the balsam).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, beginning at 2 Samuel 5:23. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.

structuredEvidence.definition: the weeping tree (some gum-distilling tree, perhaps the balsam)

firstOccurrence.englishText: When David inquired of Yahweh, he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them, and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.

timeline.evidenceText: When David inquired of Yahweh, he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them, and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then stir yourself up; for then Yahweh has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David inquired again of God; and God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle; for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”

definitions.full: H1057. baka בָּכָא noun [masculine] balsam-tree (see Arabic Dozy ZMG 1869, 188 but Löw No. 47 ; according to TA like , an eruca , compare Lane under the word; perhaps compare give little milk , of camel, i.e. drop, drip ); plural בְּכָאִים 2Sam 5:23-24 , = 1Chr 14:14-15 , singular in הַבָּכָא עֵמֶק Psa 84:7 balsam-vale , compare De Che.
